text: Survival was 8 of 12 under blue lamps and 6 of 12 under white lamps. This observation does not establish that lamp colour caused the difference because watering also differed. A comparison with the watering condition held constant would help distinguish the explanations.

Four catalogues repeat the same attribution, but all depend on one catalogue entry. That is one underlying attribution, not four independent sources. The unsigned drawing does not settle the issue. Retain the attribution as a documented hypothesis and look for a dated sketch, correspondence, or another independent basis.

The parcel has two boxes. The boxes are amber. They weigh three kilograms together.

Seven of twenty chapters are complete: 7 divided by 20 is 35%. Replace the summary with '7 of 20 chapters are complete (35%).' Half would be 10 chapters, so the supplied claim overstates the recorded progress.

The dotted A-to-C link represents a proposed relation, not a confirmed observation. Revise the caption accordingly and retain the dotted line unless separate evidence justifies changing its status. The legend supplies the correction; no new evidence is implied.

The handoff is evidence of another reader's inspection of q8, not my inspection of q9. A's earlier result may be carried forward only after confirming the stated identity; B needs a fresh inspection because it was replaced. Keep the old batch reference and the new work separately attributed.

I will resume with the caption check described in the note. The outline remains recorded as accepted, while illustration review stays pending. The note provides the checkpoint; it does not mean I have already checked the captions or that work continued during the gap.
The lantern waits beneath the blue stair.
Entry A: paper; Entry B: clay; Entry C: wood.

The open gate can suggest welcome or available access. The departing footsteps complicate that invitation and can suggest absence, refusal, or a missed encounter. The two lines do not settle whose footsteps they are or why they turned away. Both readings should retain that unresolved relationship.

'Here I wait' can carry either acceptance or impatience. A slow cadence and images of settled attention would support acceptance; repeated interruptions or an approaching deadline would support impatience. Compare those features in the surrounding poem rather than assign the speaker's state from the closing sentence alone.

The preview renders correctly, but the downloadable package has not been produced. Delivery is not complete. The next required result is the package itself, followed by a check that it opens and contains the intended files; a successful preview alone does not establish that result.

A harbor bell travels across the water.
The far shore keeps its line of lamps.
One returning note thins beside the pier.
The rope rests against the weathered post.
Which shore receives the sound as home?

The stone keeps the morning cool.
A darker seam remembers where rain passed.
A leaf rests where the shadow ends.
The path continues past the wall.
